source.title: Soft Prompt Threats: Attacking Safety Alignment and Unlearning in Open-Source LLMs through the Embedding Space
source.authors: Leo Schwinn; David Dobre; Sophie Xhonneux; G. Gidel; Stephan Günnemann

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure/table text has OCR or layout corruption, but the relevant prose and tabulated results are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether adversarial embedding-space attacks can recover information from unlearned models, using an attack and recovery measure different from the cited unlearning methods.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's unlearning evaluations and their no-attack references. The separate safety-alignment, jailbreak-generation, and pretraining-data-extraction experiments do not test the claim about recovering knowledge from unlearned models. Table 1 does not clearly disaggregate its displayed attack values by the All/Last layer modes mentioned in the prose; no layer-specific values are inferred.
record.test_reason: The study attacks existing unlearned models: the Who's Harry Potter model (LlamaHP) and TOFU models unlearned with gradient ascent (GA) and gradient difference (GD). It uses white-box embedding-space attacks, top-k sampling, and the logit-lens baselines HPA and PDA. It measures how much supposedly forgotten knowledge is recovered. This bears on version A's claim that simple attacks don't recover the knowledge. It uses a different method from the original evaluations (T2). Embedding perturbation is neither fine-tuning (B), activation-direction ablation (C), quantization (D) nor prompting only (E).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that embedding-space attacks extract considerably more supposedly deleted information than direct prompts from LlamaHP and from TOFU GA/GD models. On HP Q&A, recovery reaches near-original accuracy (30.9% vs 34.5%). They present the attacks as an interrogation tool for unlearning, alongside the separate safety-alignment findings.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates existing Harry Potter unlearning and TOFU gradient-ascent/gradient-difference models, but uses optimized continuous embedding perturbations and cumulative recovery measures rather than reproducing the original unlearning recipes or their evaluations.
record.method_sensitivity: Harry Potter attack results vary with individual versus universal attack, attacked-token count, and attack configuration; fewer attacked tokens and universal attacks generally perform better. TOFU reports different values by unlearning method, individual/universal attack, token count, and train/test split.

fits_no_version.finding: A universal embedding attack on base Llama3-8B raises ROUGE-1 for completing held-out Harry Potter book sentences from 0.11 to 0.22.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Embedding-space attacks extract pretraining data from non-unlearned models.

record.problems: The Harry Potter evaluation is a custom 55-question dataset; reported attack values are cumulative and Table 1 does not clearly separate the All/Last layer configurations. The TOFU results use a 1% forget set and report cumulative ROUGE-1 rather than a direct measure of exact fact accuracy; no uncertainty estimates are given for these recovery results. The text and Appendix K narrative/table are inconsistent about some TOFU score descriptions (the appendix prose says up to 0.41, while Table 6 reports values up to 0.52). Authors also note that correct factuality is not evaluated for affirmative-response attacks in their broader experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant unlearning-recovery rows omitted. Non-unlearning safety-alignment attacks, jailbreak-generation tests, toxicity/perplexity results, and pretraining-data extraction were excluded as outside the claim versions.

untested.parts: General-ability retention of the unlearned models is not measured. WMDP and the methods used in it (e.g. RMU) are not tested.
No relearning or fine-tuning of unlearned models.
No activation-direction ablation. Layer-wise decoding (App. H) is not an ablation and makes no block-versus-delete argument.
No rephrasing, jailbreak-prompt, multilingual or in-context recovery test on unlearned models.
No robust unlearning method is evaluated.

missing.what: Held-out universal-attack generalization on HP Q&A, split into All/Last layers. 50/50 split: 17.9/14.3 at 1 token. 25/75 split: 28.6/23.8 at 1 token; lower values at 5 and 20 tokens.
TOFU sampling analysis for one forget-set question over 1024 samples. Greedy information leak is about 0.381 for both methods; GD gives high-leak answers more often.
The appended Table 1 labels the embedding-attack value 25.5 as 'only last layer'. The main Table 1 values may mix All and Last modes; layer mode per value needs resolving.

record.verdict_notes: All rows carried the invalid version 'V1' and are relinked to A. States are judged against A's robustness claim: 'absent' means the knowledge was not kept suppressed under attack. HP comparisons partly pit cumulative (20-attempt or 100-sample) success against one-shot baselines, which favours recovery. The authors note answer correctness under affirmative-target attacks may include hallucination, though the HP metric is keyword-based. The TOFU metric is described as 'minimum' ROUGE over responses, likely meaning maximum. Appendix K prose ('up to 0.41') conflicts with Table 6 (up to 0.52). Not an original source; it tests the original Who's Harry Potter model.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures targeted-knowledge recovery after unlearning but does not assess general-ability retention as part of that unlearning evaluation, nor test all unlearning methods or attack types in the claim.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning on a small set of unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation and no mechanistic test establishing that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge. Multilayer decoding is not an ablation.
No recovery test using prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information alone.
No newer unlearning method is evaluated for resistance to the specified attacks.

relationships.condition: LlamaHP (Who's Harry Potter) on custom 55-question HP Q&A, embedding-space attacks and top-k sampling
relationships.reason: Accuracy recovers from 3.6% to 20–30.9% (HP-ind-1/5/20, HP-univ-1/5/20). Sampling reaches 27.8% (HP-topk) and the combined attack 38.2%, versus 34.5% for the original (HP-embed-topk).
relationships.display_finding: Embedding attacks raised accuracy from 3.6% to 20–30.9%, sampling reached 27.8%, and their combination reached 38.2% versus 34.5% for the original model.

relation.reason: Its own results bear directly on whether unlearning resists attacks.

tranche.reason: A different attack method (embedding-space attacks, cumulative metrics) on existing unlearned models (WHP, TOFU GA/GD), aimed at the same question.

source_check.notes: Main Table 1 prose mentions an All/Last split, but the table shows one value per cell. The appended Table 1 labels 3.6/25.5/7.2/9.0 as last layer only. Attacked values are cumulative over 20 evaluations or 100 samples; the 34.5 original is one-shot. TOFU ROUGE is defined as the 'minimum' ROUGE-1 over responses, probably a slip for maximum. App. K prose says ROUGE 'increases up to 0.41', but Table 6 shows 0.46-0.52.

statements.correction: LlamaHP, custom 55-question HP Q&A: HPA (logit lens) 7.2 and PDA (layer-wise probability deltas) 9.0, versus 3.6 unattacked and 34.5 for the original Llama2. Top-k sampling (100 samples, temperature 2) gives CU 27.8. Embedding attacks give 20-30.9.
statements.problem: Gives no numbers for this study and cites HP-HPA/HP-PDA as input-side or sampling attacks with no weight access. HPA and PDA are logit-lens attacks that read intermediate layers, so they need internal access. HP Q&A is not among the stated WMDP/TOFU settings. They lift accuracy only slightly. On the same model, top-k sampling alone reaches 27.8%, which cuts against the 'sampling' part.

statements.correction: Optional addition: LlamaHP HP Q&A, HPA 7.2 vs universal 1-token embedding attack 30.9, from 3.6 unattacked (original 34.5).
statements.problem: Nothing wrong. The text names no result from this study, though it cites rows HP-HPA and HP-univ-1, which fit the factor (attack type).
